newsitem.title: USA: India 96/97 vegoil imports 1.3 MMT--US ag attache.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 vegoil imports 1.3 MMT--US ag attache.

text.p: India was expected to import 1.3 million tonnes of vegetable oil during the 1996/97 marketing year, a 100,000-tonne increase on the previous year, the U.S. agriculturual attache in New Dehli said in a report released Monday.
The attache also said rapeseed production in 1996/97 was likely to be a record 6.3 million tonnes.
"Good winter weather conditions have helped to offset the effects of a dry December on yields," the attache said.
Indian importers were purchasing "record volumes of sunflower oil which is trading at a discount to palm olein," the report said.

"Vegetable oil imports during 1996/97 are expected to be somewhat higher than last year's 1.2 MMT due to the widening gap between domestic production and consumption," the attache wrote. "Imports and commitments during October - March are estimated at 550,000 tonnes compared to 450,000 tonnes during the corresponding period in 1995/96."
India's agriculture minister opposes import of soybeans and recently said recently a ban on imports would not be lifted and the import duty on vegetable oil should be raised from 20 to 30 percent.
"Subsequently some lower level Ministry of Agriculture officials indicated that limited quantities of soybean imports might be permitted if phytosanitary issues can be resolved," the attache said.

Soybean processors in India have lobbied vigorously for soybeans to be imported, subject to re-export of soybean meal, so the industry can better utilitize excess capacity and build India's role as an exporter of value-added goods.
Soybean mills were estimated to be capable of handling between 11 and 13 million tonnes a year, compared to a crop of less than four million tonnes.
